item: 2017 NFL Personnel (Injury) Report Policy PDF
detail: The policy document that every secondary source cites for injury-designation definitions returned HTTP 404 ('FLAG ON THE PLAY') from operations.nfl.com on 2026-11-14. Consequently this site does not quote the policy text and does not assert what 'Questionable' or 'Doubtful' officially mean. Only the categories observed on the live report are recorded.
action: No definition text published. Category labels reproduced exactly as observed.

item: League-wide depth charts page
detail: https://www.nfl.com/depth-charts/ returns HTTP 404. There is no league-wide official depth chart at that address. All depth information on this site therefore comes from club sites or from roster status codes, and is labelled DERIVED.
action: Depth presented as a derived layer only, never as official.

item: Football Operations injury-report landing page
detail: https://operations.nfl.com/health-safety/injury-report/ returns HTTP 404. An official policy landing page could not be located at this path.
action: None. Recorded for completeness.

item: Myles Garrett — club attribution
detail: NFL.com's Week 10 injury report lists Myles Garrett as an LB on the Los Angeles Rams with a knee designation and a 'resting player' note. NFL.com's Next Gen Stats front page carries a 2026 Rams article titled 'Rams' Sean McVay: No timeline on Myles Garrett's return post knee surgery', and a separate NFL.com article is headlined 'How does Myles Garrett fit into Rams defense?'. These agree on the Rams but the injury-row note mixes a real knee injury with a rest designation, which the site will not attempt to untangle. No resolution applied.
action: Row published verbatim as captured. Both sources linked.

item: Aaron Donald — listed as a non-participant while shown as active
detail: The Week 10 Rams injury table lists Aaron Donald (DT) as 'Did Not Participate In Practice' with no injury and no game status. NFL.com's own player profile for Aaron Donald shows him as an active Los Angeles Rams DE with 11 years of experience, and an NFL.com article states he unretired on Aug. 30 and planned a season debut. Both are official NFL.com pages and they cannot both be read at face value. No resolution applied.
action: Row published verbatim. Profile linked alongside.

item: Four clubs absent from the Week 10 injury snapshot
detail: The captured Week 10 injury report covers 28 of 32 clubs. Chicago, Denver, Tampa Bay and Philadelphia are absent. All 28 clubs that do appear also appear in the 14-game Week 10 schedule capture. Whether those four clubs are on a bye or their reports were simply not posted at capture time could not be confirmed, because no official 2026 bye-week table was verified in this session.
action: Counts are always stated as 'x of 28 captured clubs', never as a league total.

item: One Week 10 game was already final at capture time
detail: Washington at New York Giants kicked off Thursday 2026-11-12 and finished 24-21. Their injury tables are still shown in the Week 10 report. Using those rows as a pre-game signal would be look-ahead bias. They are the completed game's report, not a forecast input.
action: Flagged so no analysis treats the completed game's rows as forward-looking.

item: No benchmark price source exists in this repository
detail: The league publishes results, statistics and schedules but not betting prices. No odds feed, historical closing line, or graded result set is present or was licensed for this session. Every edge, expected-value and closing-line-value field on this site is therefore blank. Nothing has been estimated or imputed to fill them.
action: All price, edge and EV fields left blank and labelled. See question Q03 and suggestion SG01.

item: No official snap counts available
detail: Determining that a second- or third-string player actually replaced a starter requires snap share. No snap-count feed was located or verified. The deficiency model therefore reports official absence designations only, and does not claim that any specific backup played.
action: Deficiency magnitude left blank. See question Q05 and suggestion SG04.

item: Club depth charts are self-described as unofficial
detail: The one club depth chart captured in full is headed 'Kansas City Chiefs Unofficial Depth Chart' by the club itself. Its ordering is reproduced exactly, but it is not an official league ranking and must not be presented as one.
action: Labelled DERIVED / UNOFFICIAL wherever it appears.

item: Player-name collisions make name joins unsafe
detail: Two different players named Marcus Harris appear in the captured data: a Tennessee cornerback and a Kansas City defensive tackle. NFL player URLs disambiguate them with numeric suffixes, but plain names do not. Any join performed on player name alone will silently merge distinct people.
action: Rows kept separate. Any future join must key on the player URL, not the display name.

item: Legal and regulatory sources not verified
detail: No gambling-regulator, tax or gaming-commission source was loaded or verified during this session. The site therefore makes no statement about legality, licensing or tax treatment in any jurisdiction, including the user's location. Nothing on this site is a bet, an offer to wager, or bookmaking.
action: Legal question recorded as open (Q14) and left unanswered. Leaderboard rewards kept non-monetary (SG11).

item: Terms of use for automated fetching not reviewed
detail: Every capture in this session was a single page load. The terms of use and robots policy of nfl.com and of the 32 club sites were not reviewed, so no statement is made about whether scheduled automated collection would be permitted.
action: No scheduled collector was built. See question Q18.

item: Single-season, single-snapshot dataset
detail: All data here comes from one 2026 season and, for injuries, one capture on one day. Nothing on this site has a multi-season history, so no claim of persistence over time can be made and no backtest has been run.
action: Every strategy is marked NOT RUN or BLOCKED. No performance figure is displayed.

item: A parallel session's injury CSV had a column-shift bug on multi-injury cells
detail: A concurrent session independently transcribed the same Week 10 report into data/injuries.csv. Comparing the two transcriptions row by row: all 161 rows it contains also appear in this repo's 345-row capture, with no row present only in theirs. 156 of 161 rows match field for field, which is a useful independent confirmation of the capture. The 5 that differed all involve a player with two listed body parts: 'Ankle, Knee', 'Wrist, Chest', 'Knee, Achilles', 'Ankle, Triceps' and 'Ankle, Knee'. Because that CSV was comma-delimited and the injury field was unquoted, the second body part shifted into the adjacent columns, so the practice and game status fields were displaced. This repo's capture preserves the full published value and the correct game status, and the raw page capture confirms it (e.g. A.J. Brown 'Ankle, Knee / Limited Participation / Questionable').
action: This repo keeps its own capture, which was verified line by line against the raw page. The other session's files are preserved in archive/v2/ for reference. Any future CSV export must quote every field containing a comma.

item: Houston Texans depth chart published as an image
detail: https://www.houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart loads, but the chart itself is rendered as an image inside a photo-gallery widget rather than as a position table. No player names are machine-readable. Houston is therefore the only club of 32 with no depth chart on this site. The Texans roster page does publish a readable table, but it is ordered alphabetically, not by depth, so it cannot be substituted without inventing the string ordering. Depth is an ordering, and the ordering is the fact being reported.
action: Houston is absent from the Backup Depth page and counted as uncovered. Nothing inferred in its place.

item: Player-prop correlations are computed estimates from a third-party mirror
detail: data/prop-correlations-d.csv coefficients are computed from nflverse player_stats 1999-2024 via the Beexly/Sports mirror (file commit 2026-11-07), QA-gated (schema, coverage, 100% score join vs games.csv, distribution sanity, deterministic rebuild). They are model inputs, NOT official NFL statistics, and must not be presented as verified league facts. The source parquet is not committed and its prior workspace-only path is absent from this checkout; therefore the prop-correlation rebuild check V9 is BLOCKED here. The existing coefficients remain third-party-derived and were not independently regenerated in this run.
action: Retain the third-party label; for reproducible refreshes, fetch a pinned source artifact and record its content hash. Until that input and QA run are available, treat V9 as BLOCKED and do not claim this checkout independently reproduced the estimates.

item: Opening prices exist for exactly one season, from one book, with no odds - so requirement 1 is met on the close side only
detail: The price store records an opening number for 272 games (2021, sportsbook WSGT, spreads and totals, no odds) and closes for 6,830 games (2006-2018) plus 7,439 line records on the games feed. Every other season has no first-posted price in any capture this repository holds. The store publishes the gap as coverage rather than filling it: 56,624 of 78,410 snapshots carry the vintage UNDOCUMENTED.
action: Requirement 1 is recorded as PARTIALLY MET on requirements.html terms: the store holds opening AND closing columns for every market, and the opening column is blank where no dated open exists. Closing the gap needs the live snapshot collector (SG16); no third-party archive is substituted for it.

item: A quarter of the backtest log is priced at an assumed -110 because the feed carries a line with no odds
detail: 3,423 of 13,310 published bets (25.7%) are struck against a spread or total number for which the games feed publishes no payout. Those rows carry price_basis NOT_POSTED_ASSUMED_-110. The signal block is unaffected (it never reads a stake or a price); the ROI column for those rules is an approximation and is marked as such in the same table as the 100%-posted moneyline rules.
action: Published in the staking block next to 'priced at a number the feed holds' and in the roi_is_assumed column; the -110 assumption is never presented as a market quote.

item: Two feeds disagree with each other and neither is declared authoritative: 167 games have opposite favourites
detail: games.csv vs sc_lines: 2,105 of 4,142 comparable side rows differ, median 0.5 pt, max 11.0, and the sign disagrees on 167 games (e.g. 2013_01 WAS_SD: +7.0 against -7.0). closing_lines vs games.csv moneyline odds agree on 394 of 3,232. initial_lines vs games.csv disagree on 61 of 272. Nothing here averages, picks a winner, or reconciles by authority.
action: Published as a drift matrix on price-store.html and used as the reason one feed is quarantined; recorded so a reader can see the size of the vendor disagreement before trusting any single number.

item: 38 scheduled 2026 games carry no line in any captured feed, 16 of them in the current Week 11 slate
detail: Week 11 (2026-11-19/22) has 16 games and none has a spread, total or moneyline in the capture; the whole season has 272 games of which 234 are lined. For those games the market column on the origination board is blank, so the difference column is blank too - a line can be originated against nothing.
action: Board rows published with the market column marked 'no market number captured'; delta left blank rather than measured against an assumed hold.

item: The store's phase vocabulary cannot express 'the source never said when this price was taken'
detail: engine/price_snapshots.py constrains phase to open/close/intermediate. 57,920 of 78,410 snapshots in this session's ledger are rejected by that CHECK - not because they are bad rows but because labelling an undated number 'intermediate' would invent a provenance the feed does not have.
action: Recorded as a request on COORDINATION.md rather than patched here (that file is another session's): either a fourth phase value is added to the CHECK, or the store stays close-only and the ledger remains a separate export. Decision sits with the storage owner and Q11.

item: The 2026 season in the captured feed stops at Week 9 plus one Week 10 game, and the official standings row for 2026 shows 16-1
detail: data/results.tsv (transcribed from the official Week-by-week pages, S04/S49) contains 137 games: weeks 1-4 have 16 games, weeks 5 and 9 have 15, weeks 6-8 have 14, week 10 has 1. That is the feed's state at the capture moment, not an error in this repository, but it means 'current' on this site means 2026-11-14 and nothing later. The season recount matches the official 2026 standings for 32 of 32 clubs, which is what makes the shortfall a coverage fact rather than a correctness one.
action: Every dated page states the capture date; the ledger row for each game records which of the two feeds it was verified against.

item: No bet in this repository can be measured for closing-line value, so the promotion gate that needs CLV cannot run and no reward can be paid
detail: CLV needs the price at the time the pick was made and the close after it. The capture has no dated open, so 0 of 13,310 bets are measurable. This session's demotion run therefore evaluates D1 against the recorded market line as a named substitute (D1-SUBSTITUTE) and reports the substitution on the page rather than presenting it as the original rule.
action: demotion-gate.html publishes the substitute definition, the numbers, and the exact unlock (the snapshot collector). Rewards: 0 units paid, 9 of 9 rules ineligible - stated on signal-vs-staking.html.

item: The model's own signal is negative against the market on all three markets, and worse as the threshold tightens
detail: Walk-forward, 2011-2026, 13,310 bets: side rules lose 1.98 to 4.96 points per bet vs the recorded market line (3,364 bets at a 1.0-point gap), and both total rules are inverted - calibration slope -0.02 to -0.07, i.e. a bigger stated gap predicts a worse result. Moneyline rules are -0.017 to -0.020 probability points.
action: Published as the headline of the leaderboard rather than hidden in a footnote; nothing is promoted, so nothing is exposed to the negative edge. The tuning grid that chose these parameters is published with the model card.

item: Three of the four line files have no field documentation at all - only filenames assert what they are
detail: Upstream DATASETS.md documents the games feed (result = home-away; total = sum; spread_line positive = home favoured) and does not document closing_lines.csv, sc_lines.csv, initial_lines.csv or win_totals.csv. The publisher's own code (code/draft_kings.R) scrapes live DraftKings prices for unplayed games, which explains current-season movement but is not documentation of the historical columns. No CRAN reference page for these functions is reachable.
action: The store records the vintage claim as 'filename only' in the vintage_evidence column of every snapshot row, and pages print UNDOCUMENTED rather than guessing a market hour.

item: This session refreshed one capture, and the diff is 26 fields - all moneylines of games that have not been played
detail: data/raw/games.csv at main was 9 days behind upstream. 7,548 games on both sides, 0 added or removed; the difference is 26 rows' moneyline columns (13 games x 2 sides), e.g. 2026_10_HOU_CLE home moneyline -230 -> -225. Scores, spreads and totals are unchanged, so no historical settlement in this repository moves.
action: Refreshed file committed with its new sha256 in the manifest and the previous hash recorded alongside it, so the change is auditable rather than silent.
